new_statements.quote: In many cases, stress is insensitive to weight; in some languages, stress location is sensitive to morphosyntactic factors. One [Torricelli; Sandaun, PNG] regularly assigns stress to the penultimate syllable, but verbs allow for stress on either syllable of the final foot, resulting in contrasts such as [ˈte.re] ‘chop’ and [te.ˈre] ‘howl’. While forms like the noun [ˈte.li] ‘round thing’ would be equally legitimate for a verb, *[te.ˈli] with final stress is not a possible noun.

new_statements.rule_in_words: In One, word stress is regularly penultimate; in verbs (only) stress may fall lexically on either syllable of the final foot, so verbs show penult vs final minimal pairs, while nouns are always penultimate. Statement is for 'One' generically as described by co-author Donohue from his own fieldwork, which (Donohue 2000 fn.1) is the Molmo village variety (molm1235); Kwamtim One is not named.
new_statements.exceptions: Verbs: lexical choice between penultimate and final stress within the final foot ([ˈte.re] 'chop' vs [te.ˈre] 'howl'); nouns do not allow final stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level stress on citation forms (disyllables cited); weight-insensitive by implication of the surrounding text. Handbook survey chapter, but the One data are the co-author's own (first-hand), so not strictly second-hand; however it describes Donohue's One (= Molmo One), a sister lect of Kwamtim One under Glottolog's six-way split of One.
new_statements.identity_note: No source opened describes Kwamtim One (kwam1254, Kwamtim village) specifically. The quoted stress statement is for 'One' as used by Donohue, which he defines (Donohue 2000 fn.1) as the Molmo village variety = Molmo One, molm1235 (already checked under that glottocode, whose folder holds the same file). Glottolog/ISO split One into six languages (Northern, Inebu, Kabore, Kwamtim, Molmo, Southern One) following Crowther 2001; Donohue & Crowther 2005 and BDF 2021 treat One as one language with varieties. Applying the Molmo rule to Kwamtim would be an inference across sister lects, hence not proposed for the catalog to avoid a duplicate entity of record.
